title: Merge PowerPoint – Combine PPTX Files Free, No Upload
description: Merge PowerPoint presentations into one PPTX in your browser: put the decks in order and keep text, pictures, charts and notes. Free, no upload.
heading: Merge PowerPoint presentations
subtitle: Combine two or more PowerPoint presentations into one .pptx file, in the order you choose; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Merge PPTX files online without PowerPoint (beta): add two or more presentations, drag them into order and download one .pptx. The files are edited directly rather than redrawn, so the slides keep their text, pictures, tables, charts, video and speaker notes. Every slide takes the first presentation's theme and slide size. Works with .pptx, .ppsx and .potx files. Your files never leave your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is handled by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Notes and media kept
features.text: Slides keep their text, pictures, tables, charts, video and speaker notes.

features.title: Your order
features.text: Drag the presentations into the order you want; the slides follow it.

steps.title: Choose your presentations
steps.text: Click Choose a file, or drop two or more .pptx, .ppsx or .potx files on the page.

steps.title: Put them in order
steps.text: Drag the presentations into order. The first one sets the theme and slide size.

steps.title: Merge and download
steps.text: Click Merge, then download the combined .pptx file.

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I combine two PowerPoint presentations?
faq.answer: Two presentations are combined by copying the slides of one into the other: PowerPoint's Reuse Slides does this, and Keynote, LibreOffice Impress and Google Slides' slide import can do the same. On this page, add both files, drag them into order and click Merge; you get one .pptx, made in your browser without uploading.

faq.question: Will the slides keep their design?
faq.answer: Mostly. Every slide takes the first presentation's theme, so slides from a deck with another theme use its matching layout and may change colour or font. Open the merged file in the PowerPoint viewer to check it.

faq.question: What if my presentations have different slide sizes?
faq.answer: The merged file uses the first presentation's slide size. Slides from a 4:3 deck in a 16:9 one, or the other way round, are not rescaled, so their content may sit off-centre or run past the edge.

faq.question: Are speaker notes and videos kept?
faq.answer: Yes. The files are edited directly, so each slide keeps its speaker notes, pictures, tables, charts and video.

faq.question: Can I merge the slides into one PDF instead?
faq.answer: Merge the presentations here, then save the result with PowerPoint to PDF, one page per slide.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
